newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Mobile phone joins ranks of Vietnam status symbols.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phone joins ranks of Vietnam status symbols.

text.p: Vietnam, one of the world's poorest countries and where ownership of a water buffalo is still considered a rural status symbol, said on Friday that mobile phone usage was soaring.

The official Vietnam News Agency reported that the number of users nationwide stood at 115,000 as of the end of June. In early 1996, the figure was close to 20,000. By the end of the year it stood at 63,000.
VNA said two national mobile networks, VMS and Vinaphone, accounted for around 100,000 users, while a Ho Chi Minh City-based service, Call Link, had 15,000 subscribers.
It added that a fourth company, the Saigon Telecommunications stock company, had been licensed to join the fray and was expected to begin operations later this year.
Mobile phones have fast acquired the prestige of a status symbol in Vietnam, despite the costs in a country where per capita income is less than $300 a year.
But according to U.S. and Foreign Commercial Service data, the majority of users are members of the ruling Communist Party or employees of state-owned firms.
A report issued in May said 60 percent of users were state employees or workers at government ministries, while the balance belonged to private business and foreign firms.
Industry estimates say the number of users is expected to approach 150,000 by the end of this year and reach half a million by 2005.
